newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end sharply higher.

text.p: CME lean hog and pork belly futures finished sharply higher on short covering and commercial buying prompted by an oversold condition and expected stronger cash hog markets, traders said.
Live hogs closed 1.150 to 0.075 cent per lb higher with June up 0.775 at 80.875 cents. Pork bellies ended up 1.900 to 2.250 with July up 2.125 at 88.500 cents.

Stronger-than-expected cash hog markets Monday and calls for higher cash markets Tuesday reinforced support linked to oversold condition and boosted hog futures. Commercial support pushed prices up into early buy stops, traders said.

Hog marketings apparently became current last week and hog numbers are expected to tighten this summer on a seasonal basis, several sources noted. Also, Japan is expected to step up its pork buying on the world market, especially since Taiwan's pork ban is still in effect.
The outlook is for firming cash pork product prices after losses last week, they said.

"The seasonal tendency is that (hog) numbers start to tighten up and I think the feeling (is) that maybe we could see the Japanese come into the market," said Don Roose, President U.S. Commodities Inc.

Rand Financials and Lind-Waldock notably bought June and July while E.D.& F. Man sold June. R.J. O'Brien bought July and Cargill Investor Services bought August. In hog options, one local bought October 72 puts on the early rally while commission houses were on both sides of August 82 and 84 calls and Refco sold June 81 calls. Rand sold October 78 and 80 calls late, pit sources said.

Pork bellies also ran up on buy stops which were triggered by short covering. Gains were further bolstered by indications futures were oversold and that hog marketings and ensuing slaughter would tighten as the summer months unfold. Light stored belly stocks and technical strength also offset weak cash pork belly prices, traders said.

LFG turned buyer late after selling early and helped push prices up through a gap left in the charts last week, traders said. Locals took profits late which pared gains but scattered demand curbed declines. Prudential Securities and E.D.&F. Man sold late, pit sources said.
